disposition: INCOMPLETE + CONFOUNDED — NOT SEALED. Mints neither pass nor fail for the resurfacing hypothesis. No comparative verdict.
correction_note: Supersedes the earlier framing in this file's history: common boot exposure of the target rule in all three arms was the REGISTERED CONTROL, not a confound. The intended estimand is whether reactivating an already-boot-loaded rule at the consequential boundary beats boot exposure alone (A) and generic recency (C). The sole confound was the planning turn, not the boot map.

registered_design.estimand: After a rule is loaded at boot, does reactivating the applicable rule at the consequential boundary outperform boot exposure alone and generic recency?
registered_design.A: common boot map (target rule present) + neutral length-matched boundary
registered_design.B: common boot map (target rule present) + exact applicable constraint at boundary
registered_design.C: common boot map (target rule present) + irrelevant valid length-matched constraint at boundary
registered_design.protocol: two-turn: plan, then implement on go signal; K=5/condition

causal_status.aborted_candidates: 6, missing rather than failed (provider credit exhaustion)
causal_status.completed_outcomes: 9 of 9 pass (10/10 hidden grader, graded deterministically by the opus main loop; solver off scoring path)
causal_status.primary_confound: uncontrolled target-rule articulation during planning — every planner (A, B, C alike) restated the boot-loaded target rule in its turn-1 plan, a second activation before the registered boundary manipulation; the boot-only and recency-control arms self-administered the treatment

correct_rerun.principle: preserve common boot exposure; remove the uncontrolled self-resurfacing. Do NOT switch to bare-boot first-time injection — that tests just-in-time instruction, a different mechanism.
correct_rerun.A: target present at boot | planning PROHIBITED from restating it | neutral length-matched boundary
correct_rerun.B: target present at boot | planning PROHIBITED from restating it | exact applicable constraint at boundary
correct_rerun.C: target present at boot | planning PROHIBITED from restating it | irrelevant valid length-matched constraint at boundary
correct_rerun.contamination_check: before grading, inspect each planning output; if the planner quotes or materially paraphrases the target constraint before the boundary message, mark the trial 'contaminated' — neither pass nor fail, causally ineligible
correct_rerun.blocking: run balanced blocks (A1 B1 C1, A2 B2 C2, ...) so an early credit stop yields complete blocks, not A=5 B=3 C=1
correct_rerun.separate_second_experiment: the planner-self-resurfacing observation ('does self-generated articulation reactivate a boot-loaded constraint?') is worth testing, but as a SEPARATE run after the clean external-resurfacing run — not as another arm now

incidental_signal_hypothesis_only: same item, single-turn spec+scaffold (CLAUDE-2 replay04) = 1/3 vs two-turn plan-first here = 5/5. Consistent with self-articulation-during-planning reactivating the rule — this is the separate second experiment above, not a result.
